features: generation, monotonic-time, replay, and tamper protection

limitations: The contract evaluates caller-supplied path evidence and does not execute or prevent OS actions by itself; an enforcement adapter must bind the receipt to trusted policy enforcement.
Risk labels and action labels are explicit caller inputs; the module does not infer risk from model output or content.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes real model serving, network, memory, accelerator, or kernel scheduler performance.
The real-task scenarios are deterministic control-plane fixtures, not evidence of general intelligence, model quality, browser autonomy, robotics, or production agent efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
objective: Add provider-neutral fail-closed runtime governance that evaluates ordered agent actions against the observed execution path, path-sensitive rules, bounded risk budgets, approval requirements, terminal evidence linkage, replay/tamper fences, and non-authority boundaries without executing actions or contacting external services.

research_inputs.finding: Dynamo separates prefill and decode, uses KV-aware worker selection, transfers backend-specific metadata, and supports runtime worker registration and drain-based removal.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL remains provider-neutral and records ordered action/resource evidence rather than importing backend metadata or treating serving claims as authority.

research_inputs.finding: Durable agent execution must survive transient API failures, application errors, restarts, asynchronous workflows, and human-in-the-loop pauses.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Path decisions are immutable, replay-protected, generation-fenced, and linkable to terminal result and trace digests.

research_inputs.finding: Runtime governance must evaluate a proposed action against the partial execution path and organizational state because individually permitted steps can form a prohibited sequence.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds ordered path steps, path-sensitive rule matching, bounded risk budgets, approval gates, actor-transition fencing, and deterministic admission receipts.

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the path-governance module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged migration release
